sentences.text: Laquintasaura is the genus name for this extinct dinosaur, recognized as a small and very primitive animal known for its distinct dental anatomy.
Researchers describe it as a small, dog-sized animal that walked on its two hind legs, with a total length not exceeding one meter.
It possessed a bird-like hip bone and is assumed to have been a lithe bipedal runner.
Prepared material included isolated cranial remains, many teeth, the four main types of vertebrae, a scapula, pelvic material, hind limb material, and other isolated postcranial elements.
However, forelimb material was completely absent and foot material was very limited in the collection.
This species holds the distinction of being the first dinosaur identified from Venezuela.
The largest femur found in the Laquintasaura bonebed measures exactly 90 mm in length.
Bone histology analysis suggested one tibia belonged to a juvenile approximately three years old, while a scapula indicated an adult likely around ten to twelve years old.
The genus was formally described by Barrett and colleagues in 2014.
The fossils come from a single bonebed in the Early Jurassic La Quinta Formation, located in the Venezuelan part of an area now spanning Colombia and Venezuela.
Laquintasaura venezuelae is a Venezuelan ornithischian dinosaur genus containing only the type species L. venezuelae.
Laquintasaura likely lived in an alluvial plain ecosystem characterized by both arid and humid seasons.
While the dinosaur's diet consisted mainly of ferns, its dental structure suggests it could have fed on insects and small prey.
The early theropod dinosaur Tachiraptor likely lived alongside Laquintasaura and preyed upon it.

All examined Laquintasaura specimens lack fibrolamellar bone tissue, which is associated with high growth rates in other ornithischians, though conclusions about growth rates remain uncertain due to limited data and sample size.
It likely lived in groups on seasonal alluvial plains and was preyed upon by Tachiraptor.

Laquintasaura is robustly considered a basal member of Ornithischia, though taxonomic uncertainty has led to contradictory theories that it is either the base of Ornithischia or the base of the suborder Thyreophora.
There is a debate regarding whether it is an early diverging ornithischian or belongs to the subgroup Thyreophora.
A 2016 phylogenetic analysis by Baron et al. found that Laquintasaura is the sister taxon of Scutellosaurus within the clade Thyreophora, and the parent group of Laquintasaura is Thyreophora.
Laquintasaura lived during the Hettangian stage, from 201.4 to 199.5 million years ago.
As the oldest reliably dated ornithischian from the Early Jurassic, its discovery is considered very significant.
Similar dental morphotypes found in India and England date to the Middle Jurassic, over 30 million years after Laquintasaura lived.
